s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with exertional worsening and relief with forward leaning, accompanied by shortness of breath and signs of cardiac involvement
salient_findings: Sharp, stabbing right-sided chest pain worsened by exertion and relieved by leaning forward
Shortness of breath on minimal activity
Malar rash and jugular venous distension
Tender anterior chest wall and bibasilar Velcro crackles
Grade 2/6 pansystolic murmur at the left sternal border that increased with inspiration
key_facts: 44-year-old woman presented to the emergency department
2 days of sharp, stabbing right-sided chest pain
Chest pain worsened by exertion and relieved by leaning forward
Shortness of breath on minimal activity
Chronic right lower-leg swelling
Six months of symmetric wrist stiffness that improved during the day
History of heavy menstrual bleeding and a miscarriage at age 14
Chronic warfarin-refractory deep vein thromboses
Placement of a nonretrievable inferior vena cava filter
Obese and mildly tachypneic on examination
Vital signs: temperature 98.6°F, blood pressure 116/91 mm Hg, heart rate 88/min, respiratory rate 20/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Malar rash and jugular venous distension on examination
Tender anterior chest wall and bibasilar Velcro crackles on examination
Grade 2/6 pansystolic murmur at the left sternal border that increased with inspiration on examination
Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL, platelets 71 × 10^3/mm^3, ESR 55 mm/h, CRP 90.9 mg/L, D-dimer 3.7 µg/mL on laboratory studies

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Malar rash, symmetric wrist stiffness, and elevated ESR and CRP suggest autoimmune disease

shortlist.label: Infective Endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Tricuspid-valve vegetation on echocardiography and prolonged PTT suggest endocardial infection

shortlist.label: Acute Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Chest pain relieved by leaning forward and pericardial effusion on echocardiography suggest pericardial involvement

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of recurrent deep vein thromboses and miscarriage suggest antiphospholipid antibody syndrome

shortlist.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Symmetric wrist stiffness and elevated ESR and CRP suggest inflammatory arthritis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a malar rash, symmetric wrist stiffness, and elevated inflammatory markers (ESR 55 mm/h, CRP 90.9 mg/L) are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). Additionally, the patient's history of heavy menstrual bleeding, miscarriage, and chronic warfarin-refractory deep vein thromboses suggests a possible underlying autoimmune disorder, which is further supported by the presence of antiphospholipid antibodies (suggested by the history of recurrent thromboses and the presence of a non-retrievable inferior vena cava filter). The patient's cardiac findings, including the tricuspid regurgitation and pericardial effusion, can also be seen in SLE.

rejected.label: Infective Endocarditis
rejected.why: Although the patient has vegetations on the tricuspid valve, the absence of fever, negative blood cultures, and the presence of other autoimmune features make Infective Endocarditis less likely.

rejected.label: Acute Pericarditis
rejected.why: While the patient has chest pain and a pericardial effusion, the presence of other systemic symptoms and autoimmune features suggests a more complex diagnosis than isolated Acute Pericarditis.

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of recurrent thromboses and a non-retrievable inferior vena cava filter, which suggests Antiphospholipid Syndrome, this condition is often seen in the context of another autoimmune disorder, such as SLE.

rejected.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
rejected.why: The patient's symmetric wrist stiffness that improves during the day is not typical of Rheumatoid Arthritis, which usually worsens with activity.
